title: Chrome Vinyl — Millennium Electronica Splash
description: A chrome-bubble logotype erupts from a hot-magenta starburst over a spinning black vinyl record texture, anchored by a pixelated '2000' date glyph that reads exactly like a late-90s game boot screen. Where other Y2K templates lean pastel-digital, this one commits fully to the CD-insert, Daft-Punk-era chrome aesthetic.
philosophy: This template exists to recreate the precise cultural instant when electronica went mainstream — the moment a new CD slid out of its jewel case in 1999 and the cover promised the future had arrived. It values high-contrast chrome spectacle and analog-digital tension: a vinyl record (old) colliding with a pixelated splash glyph (new). It refuses anything flat, friendly, or post-2001 in sensibility — no clean grids, no readable body copy, no breathing room. The room this belongs in is dark, the speaker is about to drop something.
goodFor: Fictional electronica album or EP launch cover slides
Music event intros projected on a dark stage screen
avoidFor: Academic thesis or research paper presentations
Any context requiring legible body-copy paragraphs
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Dark-stage energy: the exact instant a jewel case snaps open and molten chrome type catches a single spotlight from above. The composition is centrifugal and dense — every element radiates outward from a single explosive center rather than resting in any calm grid, creating visual pressure that pushes toward all four edges simultaneously. Metallic gradients curve and self-reflect as though the logotype is cast from polished industrial steel, while the starburst beneath it pulses with analog warmth in violent collision with a pixelated digital overlay. Refuse any hint of breathing room, flat color, or post-millennial restraint — the slide must feel like a game boot screen and a rave flyer occupying the same physical object.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with zero outer margin — edge-to-edge visual assault, no safe-area padding. A spinning vinyl record texture occupies the entire background layer, bleeding past all four edges. The starburst detonates from a center-to-slightly-lower-center anchor, radiating outward past the frame boundary, with the chrome logotype title stacked directly over the starburst nexus and dominating the vertical midpoint. A pixelated subtitle or date glyph sits immediately below the logotype in a bottom-weighted band, and any page numeral is a tiny pixel stamp at bottom-right, nearly consumed by the surrounding texture — no header band, no footer rule, no structural chrome.

examples.promptCore: Interior spread of a late-90s electronica CD booklet: dense, dark, slightly claustrophobic with maximum spectacle. Chrome-metallic text catches directional light against a near-black vinyl-grain field, each content item reading like a track listing — short, punchy, rhythmically clustered rather than hierarchically stacked. Starburst shards or concentric groove-ring fragments intrude from at least one corner as ambient decoration. Avoid anything airy, friendly, or grid-obedient; the mood is a dark room in the three seconds before the drop.
